slot.brief: Provide a Lewis/structure figure of two simple species (e.g., one hypervalent molecule); ask students to pick the correct geometry or hybridisation from drawn options

stem: For the two species shown in the figure, the hybridisations of the central atoms, respectively, are

verdicts.working: PCl₃ has 3 bonds and 1 lone pair on P (steric number 4), so it is sp³. BrF₃ has 3 bonds and 2 lone pairs on Br (steric number 5), so it is sp³d.

working:
$\text{PCl}_3$: $3$ bond pairs $+1$ lone pair $\Rightarrow 4$ electron domains $\Rightarrow sp^3$. 
$\text{BrF}_3$: $3$ bond pairs $+2$ lone pairs $\Rightarrow 5$ electron domains $\Rightarrow sp^3d$.

Independent check: PCl₃ has 3 bonds and 1 lone pair on P (steric number 4), so it is sp³. BrF₃ has 3 bonds and 2 lone pairs on Br (steric number 5), so it is sp³d.
solution:
Hybridisation depends on the number of electron domains around the central atom.
For PCl₃: $3$ bond pairs $+1$ lone pair $=4$ domains, so hybridisation is $sp^3$.
For BrF₃: $3$ bond pairs $+2$ lone pairs $=5$ domains, so hybridisation is $sp^3d$.

figure.description: Draw two separate Lewis structures side by side, labelled PCl3 on the left and BrF3 on the right. In the left structure, place P centrally with three single P–Cl bonds, one lone pair on P, and three lone pairs on each Cl. In the right structure, place Br centrally with three single Br–F bonds, two lone pairs on Br, and three lone pairs on each F. Show all lone pairs as pairs of dots. Use clear atom labels and no geometry names.
